claim: The Production hint spells out the answer: it names the verb いきます and tells me exactly how to turn it into the target, so the card tests copying, not recall.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Grammar & Function Words / (I) want to go / Drop ます from いきます, add たいです'. Answer: いきたいです. Following the hint literally gives the answer letter for letter.
fix: Move the formation rule to the back as a note, and leave the front as '(I) want to go' (the other たい cards in this unit work with no hint).
verdictReason: Checked cards.json and the rendered faces: the card's `hint` field is 'Drop ます from いきます, add たいです' and renders on the Production front under '(I) want to go', so applying it produces いきたいです letter for letter. The other four たい citation cards (kaitai-desu-2, tabetai-desu-2, mitai-desu, aitai-desu) carry no hint and are answerable without one. The authoring rules say a hint adds a disambiguation cue and never hands over the answer; the formation rule belongs in `note` on the back.

claim: Five base-unit cards re-teach a word I already have a card for, with the same answer and nearly the same English, so I study each of these words twice as two separate cards.
evidence: dansu 'ダンス | Dance' = Lesson 15 'ダンス | Dance'. zehi-l17 'ぜひ | By all means, definitely' = Lesson 16 'ぜひ | I'd love to, by all means'. wakarimashita-l17 'わかりました | I've got that, I understand' = Lesson 8 'わかりました | Understood, I see, I understand'. oyogimasu 'およぎます | To swim' = Lesson 15 'およぎます | Swim'. shokuji-o-shimasu 'しょくじをします | To have a meal' = Lesson 16 'しょくじをします | Have a meal'.
fix: Drop the repeat cards, or keep one per word and fold any new nuance (for example ぜひ as 'definitely' with たい) into a note on the existing card.
verdictReason: The five repeats are real (ledger: ダンス and およぎます in Lesson 15, ぜひ and しょくじをします in Lesson 16, わかりました in Lesson 8) but they are deliberate: zehi-l17, shokuji-o-shimasu, oyogimasu and wakarimashita-l17 carry `repeatOf` naming the earlier card, the deck's sanctioned mechanism for a knowing repeat (src/model/index.js), and all five, dansu included, were flagged 'Possibly already taught' in their reviewNote and kept by the owner at gate 1. A repeat with one meaning is not a collision; whether to prune repeats is a deck-wide policy question for the synthesizer, not a card defect.

claim: わたしはとうきょうにすみます does not mean "I live in Tokyo": non-past すみます means "will live" (going to live there), and the present state is すんでいます.
evidence: Book: すみます is glossed "live" and is used here only as すみたいです ("want to live"); the chapter never prints すみます as a present-state statement. Card: target わたしはとうきょうにすみます, English "I live in Tokyo."
fix: Change the sentence to a wish in this chapter's frame (e.g. とうきょうにすみたいです, "I want to live in Tokyo."), or re-gloss it as a future plan ("I will live in Tokyo.").
verdictReason: Both roles flagged this card under the same id. The card is aiSuggested with no book sentence behind it. The book itself states present residence with the て-form: Lesson 24 KS1 スミスさんは とうきょうに すんでいます 'Smith-san lives in Tokyo' (chapter 51), and its glossary lists 'live すみます 165; すんでいます 229'. In Lesson 17 すみます appears only inside すみたいです. Non-past わたしはとうきょうにすみます reads as a future or intended residence, so 'I live in Tokyo.' is the wrong gloss. Either fix in the finding works; the たい rewrite keeps it inside this lesson's grammar.

claim: The card puts の between a clock time and まえに and its note states this as a rule, but with a clock time Japanese says ごじまえに; the book's noun の まえに is for events and actions.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 2: "noun の まえに verb ... Expresses what is/was done before the noun (event, action, etc.)"; every book example is an event (かいぎ, パーティー, ひるごはん). Card: ごじのまえにうちにかえりたいです, note: "A time word takes の (no) before まえに (mae ni): ごじのまえに (go-ji no mae ni), like かいぎのまえに."
fix: Replace the time with an event (e.g. ばんごはんのまえにうちにかえりたいです) and drop the "time word takes の" claim from the note.
verdictReason: aiSuggested card. The note states a rule the book does not make: GRAMMAR 2's noun before のまえに is an event or action, and every book example is one (かいぎ, パーティー, ひるごはん, しごと). A grep of all 56 cached chapters finds no clock time joined to まえ with or without の, so nothing in the book supports ごじのまえに, and the ordinary form for 'before 5:00' is ごじまえに. The target is marginal and the note's 'a time word takes の' claim is invented, which is what makes it wrong-content rather than merely unverifiable. The Reader's fix (swap the time for an event noun, drop the rule) is the safe one.

claim: Seven notes say まえに 'always follows the dictionary form', which the deck's own cards contradict: a noun takes の before まえに.
evidence: Notes on ikebana-wo-narau-mae-ni-hon, kuruma-wo-arau-mae-ni-hirugohan, shawaa-wo-abiru-mae-ni-kohii, kaigi-wo-hajimeru-mae-ni-kohii, toukyou-ni-sumu-mae-ni-uchi-wo-mitai, daunroodo-suru-mae-ni-mitai and meeru-wo-chekku-suru-mae-ni-asagohan: 'まえに (mae ni, "before") always follows the dictionary form, as in ねるまえに from Lesson 17.' Against that: base card neru-mae-ni note 'A noun needs の, as in 〜のまえに', base card no-mae-ni 'かいぎのまえに | Before the meeting', and extras cards 'パーティーのまえにシャワーをあびます', 'しごとのまえにコーヒーをのみたいです'.
fix: Change 'always follows the dictionary form' to 'a verb before まえに is in its dictionary form' in all seven notes.
verdictReason: grep -c on chapter-17-extras/cards.json finds exactly 7 notes containing 'always follows the dictionary form', on the seven ids both roles name. The book's GRAMMAR 2 (noun の まえに) and the deck's own no-mae-ni, kaigi-no-mae-ni-shiryou, wine-before-party and coffee-before-work cards contradict 'always'; base card neru-mae-ni already states the rule correctly ('A noun needs の'). One sentence rewrite applied seven times.

claim: 'that restaurant' with no 'over there' points me to そのレストラン, because the deck has always glossed あの as 'that ... over there', so I will answer with the wrong demonstrative more often than not.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Food / I want to eat at that restaurant.' Answer: 'あのレストランでたべたいです'. Earlier cards: 'あの | That (over there)', 'その | That', 'あのレストランはしずかですか | Is that restaurant over there quiet?', 'あのあおいTシャツは3,000えんです | That blue T-shirt over there is 3,000 yen.'
fix: Gloss it 'I want to eat at that restaurant over there.', matching the deck's other あの cards.
verdictReason: Checked the collection: あの is carded as 'That (over there)' and every あの sentence the learner has met before Lesson 17 except one (td-sobaichi-otera-mae-desu) carries 'over there', while その sentences are glossed plain 'that' (そのチーズケーキはおいしいですか 'Is that cheesecake delicious?', and seven more). So 'I want to eat at that restaurant.' cues その on Production and the front does not determine あの. aiSuggested card; adding 'over there' to the gloss is the deck's own convention. Later extras (ch19, 21, 22, 25) drop 'over there' too, which is a pattern for the synthesizer.

claim: This card and smith-stretch-before-sleep are the same sentence except for まいにち, so on Production I have to remember which of two almost identical fronts includes 'every day'.
evidence: neru-mae-ni-stretch: 'スミスさんはまいにちねるまえにストレッチをします | Smith-san does stretching exercises every day before going to bed.' smith-stretch-before-sleep: 'スミスさんはねるまえにストレッチをします | Smith-san does stretching exercises before going to bed.'
fix: Keep one of the two, or change the other's activity or subject so the sentences teach something different.
verdictReason: Both sentences are printed in the book: KEY SENTENCES 3 is スミスさんは まいにち ねる まえに ストレッチを します and the EXERCISES V-A example is スミスさんは ねる まえに ストレッチを します. The two Production fronts differ by 'every day', which determines whether まいにち is in the answer, so neither card is reachable by the other's prompt. Faithful to the book and not a collision.

claim: おみやげに uses に to mean 'as (a souvenir)', a use of に no earlier card taught, and the card has no note on it.
evidence: Card: 'おみやげにおかしをかいたいです | I want to buy sweets as a souvenir.', no note. The に uses I know are direction ('ぎんこうにいきます'), time ('5じに'), place of existence ('1かいにうけつけがあります'), the person an action is directed at ('たなかさんにあいます') and 'from' with もらいます. Lesson 11's おみやげ cards never used it with に.
fix: Add a note: 'Xに here means "as X" or "for X": おみやげに, as a souvenir.'
verdictReason: aiSuggested card with no note. grep of every cards.json in the collection finds おみやげに only on this card, and grep of all 56 cached book chapters finds it nowhere, so the 'as/for a souvenir' use of に is taught by neither the deck nor the book at any point. The ledger's に uses are direction, time, location, recipient and source. A one-line note is the right fix; polish stands.

claim: The sentence uses みてください, and みて (the て-form of みます) has never been taught; the deck only has fixed chunks such as みせてください and きてください.
evidence: Ledger before Lesson 17 holds ちょっとまってください, おしえてください, みせてください, まってください and きてください, but no みて. Card (aiSuggested): このえいがはぜひみてください, "Please be sure to see this movie."
fix: Rebuild with a taught form, e.g. このえいがはぜひみたいです ("I definitely want to see this movie."), or drop the card; zehi-1 already covers ぜひ + きてください.
verdictReason: Both roles flagged this card under the same id. The ledger before Lesson 17 contains no みて in any card (its ください chunks are まって, おしえて, みせて, きて); the book introduces みて as the て-form of みます in Lesson 18 (glossary 'みて see (て-form of みます) 172'; first use in chapter 42, こうじょうを みて). aiSuggested card, so it breaks the shared rule that a card uses only what this chapter or an earlier one teaches. Kept at should-fix: zehi-1 already demonstrates ぜひ + ください with a taught chunk, so the Reader's rebuild (ぜひみたいです) or a note both work.

claim: Two notes point at 'the next item' and 'the previous item', which means nothing in a shuffled deck.
evidence: mae-before-verb-station note: 'Contrast pair with the next item: まえ after a verb means 'before', while after a place it means 'in front'.' mae-front-station note: 'Contrast pair with the previous item: compare えきのまえ (in front of the station) with えきにいくまえに (before going to the station).'
fix: Name the other sentence instead of its position, e.g. 'Compare えきにいくまえに (before going to the station).'
verdictReason: Rendered faces confirm both notes verbatim: mae-before-verb-station says 'Contrast pair with the next item' and mae-front-station says 'Contrast pair with the previous item'. Anki shuffles, so the positional reference points at nothing; each note should quote the other sentence.

claim: The chapter teaches that たい states only the speaker's own wish, is not for invitations, and is impolite in a 〜たいですか question to a superior, and no card in either unit says so.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 1: "〜たい expresses the wish of the speaker and cannot be used to express the wish of anyone other than the speaker. か may be added ... but it is not appropriate for use when making an invitation. Also, it is considered impolite to use this expression when asking 〜たいですか ... especially to someone of higher status. ... it is safer to attach か to the ます-form of the verb (e.g., なにを のみますか)." Deck: seven question cards (where-eat-dinner どこでばんごはんをたべたいですか, aitai-3, ikitai-3, tabetakatta-3, mitakatta-3, ikitakunai-3, shourai-donna-tokoro-sumitai) and no note anywhere on the restriction.
fix: Add the caveat as a note on one or two of the たいですか cards (for example where-eat-dinner), saying たい is for your own wish and asking a superior 〜たいですか is rude; the ます-form + か is the safe question.
verdictReason: GRAMMAR 1 states it in three sentences (speaker's wish only, not for invitations, 〜たいですか impolite to a superior, ask with ます-form + か). grep of every cards.json in the collection for 'speaker', 'impolite', 'invitation', 'higher status', 'own wish' and 'superior' finds no note about たい; the hits are about ko-so-a, あげます/くれます and ませんか. The extras unit ships seven 〜たいですか / 〜たかったですか questions (where-eat-dinner, aitai-3, ikitai-3, tabetakatta-3, mitakatta-3, ikitakunai-3, shourai-donna-tokoro-sumitai) with no caveat on any. No excluded card covers it either.
